Byomkesh.description: The protagonist, a sharp and thoughtful detective known for his keen observation and logical reasoning.

Ajit.description: Byomkesh's close friend and chronicler, who narrates the stories and often assists in investigations.

Devkumar Babu.description: A renowned professor and scientific researcher from Calcutta, father of Habul and Rekha, and a neighbor of Byomkesh.

Habul.description: Devkumar Babu's son, a college student who admires Byomkesh and is deeply affected by his sister Rekha's death.

Rekha.description: Habul's younger sister, whose sudden and mysterious death becomes the central case in the chapter.

Dr. Rudra.description: A renowned but abrasive physician in Calcutta, known for his skill and harsh demeanor; father of Manmathanath (Nontu).

Manmathanath Rudra.description: Also called Nontu, Dr. Rudra's son, who was engaged to Rekha and is devastated by her death.

Biren Babu.description: The local police inspector (Daroga), respected by Byomkesh for his shrewdness and lack of arrogance.

Putiram.description: A servant in Byomkesh's household, occasionally mentioned in domestic contexts.

Calcutta.description: The city (now Kolkata) where the story is set, a major urban center in India.

Delhi.description: The capital city of India, where the All-India Science Congress is taking place.

All-India Science Congress.description: A major scientific conference in India attended by scientists and scholars from across the country.

India.description: The country in which the story takes place, referenced in discussions of science and national progress.

Kash.description: A type of flower (Saccharum spontaneum) mentioned metaphorically in the professor's speech.

Lakshmi.description: The Hindu goddess of wealth, invoked as a metaphor for financial resources.

Ma Kali.description: A Hindu goddess, depicted in a picture in the stepmother's room, symbolizing power and sometimes fear.

Patna.description: A city in eastern India, mentioned as the location where Devkumar Babu is to give a university lecture.

College Square.description: A well-known area in Calcutta, popular among students and referenced as a location in the story.

Punjab Mail.description: A famous express train in India, used metaphorically to describe Byomkesh's mental energy.

Babu.description: A respectful suffix or form of address for men, especially educated or upper-class individuals.

Acharyas.description: Sanskrit term for learned teachers or scholars, especially in ancient India.

Rishis.description: Sanskrit term for sages or seers, often associated with spiritual wisdom in ancient Indian tradition.

Baithak-khana.description: A sitting room or drawing room in a Bengali household.

Jhumkas.description: Traditional Indian earrings, often bell-shaped and ornate.

Sari.description: A traditional garment worn by women in India, consisting of a long piece of cloth draped around the body.

Ganga-Jamuna.description: A style of sari with a dual-tone border, named after the Ganges and Yamuna rivers.

Birenbabu.description: A respectful way to refer to Inspector Biren, combining his name with the honorific 'babu'.

Daroga.description: A term for a police inspector or officer in India.

Agnibaan.description: Literally 'arrow of fire' in Sanskrit/Hindi/Bengali, used as a chapter or section title and metaphor for sudden, fatal events.

Satyanweshi.description: A term meaning 'truth-seeker', often used to describe Byomkesh's approach to detective work.

Mantra.description: A sacred utterance or chant in Hinduism, recited for spiritual purposes.
